Rashi on Yevamot 3a:10:1.hebrew: כיון דבמקום מצות יבום הוא דאסירה - צרת הבת, וכדמפרש במתני', דמשפטרה הכתוב מזיקת ייבום, קיימא ליה באשת אח שיש לו בנים:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:10:1.english: Since it is where the mitzvah of levirate marriage applies that she is forbidden - [This refers to] the daughter's rival wife; and as explained in the Mishnah, since Scripture has exempted her from the bond of levirate marriage, she stands to him in [the status of] a brother's wife who has children.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:10:2.hebrew: שלא במקום מצוה שריא - כגון נכרי שנעשה חתנו, ולו אשה אחרת, ומת — מותרת אשתו לחמיו, כדתנן לקמן (יבמות דף יג.) גבי שש עריות חמורות מאלו במתני':
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:10:2.english: [Where it is] not in the place of a mitzvah, she is permitted - For example, an unrelated man who became his son-in-law, and he had another wife, and he died — his [other] wife is permitted to his father-in-law, as we learned later on (Yevamot 13a) in the Mishnah regarding "Six forbidden relations are more severe than these".

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:10:3.hebrew: משום הכי תנא פוטרות - דאי תנא אוסרות, משמע שהבת אוסרתה עליו ליקח, [וק"ו] שלא במקום מצוה. אבל פוטרות, לא משתמע איסורא משום צרתה של בת, אלא הבת פוטרתה מייבום, ואיסורא שכיב עלה ממילא, דהויא באיסור אשת אח שיש לה בנים. ומשום אשת אח הוא דמיתסר; שלא במקום מצוה, דליכא איסור אשת אח עלה — שריא:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:10:3.english: Because of this he taught: "They exempt" - For had he taught "they prohibit," it would imply that the daughter causes her to be forbidden to him to marry, [and all the more so] where no mitzvah applies. But "they exempt" does not imply a prohibition on account of [being] the rival wife of a daughter; rather, the daughter exempts her from levirate marriage, and the prohibition rests upon her automatically, as she remains under the prohibition of a brother's wife who has children. And it is on account of [the prohibition of] a brother's wife that she is forbidden; whereas where no mitzvah applies, where there is no prohibition of a brother's wife upon her, she is permitted.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:11:1.hebrew: וליתני מן הייבום לחודיה - דהא עיקר מצוה היא, וחליצה ממילא משתמע:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:11:1.english: And let him teach: From levirate marriage alone - For this is the primary mitzvah, and [exemption from] chalitzah is understood by itself.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:11:2.hebrew: ה"א מיחלץ חלצה - שלא להפקיע מצות ייבום, אבל יבומי לא — משום גזירת הכתוב דלצרור. קמ"ל מתני': הואיל ופטרה הבת מזיקת יבום, פטורה מן החליצה; דכל העולה לזיקת ייבום עולה לזיקת חליצה, וכל שאין עולה לזיקת ייבום פטורה מן החליצה. וכל היכא דאמרינן "חולצת ולא מתייבמת", משום ספקא הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:11:2.english: I would say she must perform chalitzah - So as not to eliminate the mitzvah of levirate marriage; but she may not enter into levirate marriage, due to the scriptural decree of "to be a rival" [Leviticus 18:18]. The mishna teaches us: Since the daughter exempted [her rival wife] from the levirate bond, she is exempt from chalitzah; for whoever is subject to the levirate bond is subject to the bond of chalitzah, and whoever is not subject to the levirate bond is exempt from chalitzah. And wherever we say that [a woman] performs chalitzah and does not enter into levirate marriage, it is [only] because of doubt.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:12:1.hebrew: וניתני ייבום ברישא - דהוא עיקר, דהא כתיב: אם לא יחפוץ האיש לקחת וחלצה (דברים כ״ה:ז׳), הא אם חפץ לייבם, מייבם — אלמא מצות ייבום ברישא:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:12:1.english: And let him teach levirate marriage first - For it is the primary [mitzvah], as it is written: "If the man does not desire to take [his brother's wife... then] she shall perform chalitzah" (Deuteronomy 25:7) — which implies that if he desires to perform levirate marriage, he performs levirate marriage; evidently, the mitzvah of levirate marriage comes first.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:12:2.hebrew: אבא שאול היא - בפ' החולץ (לקמן יבמות לט:), אבא שאול אומר: הכונס יבמתו לשום נוי ולשום אישות — כאילו פוגע בערוה, וקרוב בעיני להיות הולד ממזר:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:12:2.english: It is [in accordance with] Abba Shaul - In the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 39b), Abba Shaul says: One who marries his yevamah for the sake of beauty or for the sake of marriage — it is as if he encounters a forbidden relation [ervah], and in my eyes the offspring is close to being a mamzer.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:13:1.english: The enumeration of the first clause - Which implies fifteen and no more.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:13:2.hebrew: מנינא דסיפא - הרי אלו פוטרות, דמשמע: אלו ותו לא:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:13:2.english: The enumeration of the latter clause - [The phrase] “These exempt,” which implies: these and no more.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:1:1.english: All of them also - With regard to the exemption from levirate marriage, they are derived through an exposition from [the case of] a wife's sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:1:2.hebrew: עיקר איסורייהו - שאסורים משום ערוה בכל מקום, בהדיא כתיב בהו. אבל בתו מאנוסתו, דאיירי בה במתני', עיקר איסורה מדרשא אתיא:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:1:2.english: Their primary prohibition - That they are forbidden as an ervah in all contexts is explicitly written concerning them. However, [as for] his daughter from a woman he raped, which the mishna is dealing with — her primary prohibition is derived from a homiletical interpretation.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:2:1.hebrew: אתיא הנה הנה - לאיסורא, אתיא זמה זמה לשריפה. דבתו מאשתו, וכן בת בתו ובת בנו, ילפא מערות אשה ובתה לא תגלה, והרי בתו מאשתו בכלל בת אשתו. אבל בתו מאנוסתו לא משתמעא, דכתיב ערות אשה, ולשון אישות — דעל ידי קידושין — משמע. וגלי רחמנא בבת בתו ובת בנו מאנוסתו בהאי קרא: ערות בת בנך או בת בתך, והכא לשון אישות לא כתיב. ואכתי בתו לא כתיב הכא, וילפינן בג"ש: כתיב הכא בקרא דאנוסה כי ערותך הנה, וכתיב בקרא אחרינא דאישות שארה הנה — מה התם בתו כבת בתו, אף כאן בתו כבת בתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:2:1.english: [It is] derived [from] "they" [hena] [and] "they" [hena] - [This derivation is] for the prohibition; [and the derivation of] "wickedness" [zimah] [and] "wickedness" [zimah] is for [the penalty of] burning. For his daughter from his wife, as well as his daughter's daughter and his son's daughter, are derived from: "The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover" (Leviticus 18:17) — for behold, his daughter from his wife is included in "the daughter of his wife." However, his daughter from a woman he raped is not implied [by that verse], as it is written: "the nakedness of a woman" [ishah], and the terminology of marriage [ishut] — that is, through betrothal [kiddushin] — is implied. And the Merciful One revealed [the prohibition] regarding his daughter's daughter and his son's daughter from a woman he raped in this verse: "The nakedness of your son's daughter, or of your daughter's daughter..." (Leviticus 18:10), and here the terminology of marriage is not written. Yet still, his daughter [herself] is not written here; and we derive [it] through a gezeirah shavah [verbal analogy]: It is written here, in the verse of a raped woman: "for theirs [hena] is your own nakedness" (Leviticus 18:10), and it is written in the other verse of marriage: "they [hena] are near kinswomen" (Leviticus 18:17) — just as there, his daughter is like his daughter's daughter, so too here, his daughter is like his daughter's daughter.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:3:1.hebrew: אתיא זמה זמה - לשריפה. כתיב הכא בבתו מאשתו זמה היא, וכתיב בשריפה זמה היא באש ישרפו — מה להלן שריפה, אף כאן שריפה. ובתו מאנוסתו — הא ילפינן מהנה הנה מבת אשתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:3:1.english: It is derived [from] "zimah" [and] "zimah" - [This derivation is] for [the punishment of] burning. It is written here, regarding his daughter from his wife: "It is wickedness" [Leviticus 18:17], and it is written regarding [the punishment of] burning: "It is wickedness; they shall be burnt with fire" [Leviticus 20:14] — just as there [the punishment is] burning, so too here [the punishment is] burning. And [as for] his daughter from a raped woman — behold, we derive [her law] from "henah" "henah" from his wife's daughter.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:4:1.english: Let him teach [a] wife's sister last - For all of them are derived from it with regard to the exemption from levirate marriage below.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:5:1.hebrew: להאי בבא - כל איסור [אחוותא] ליתני לבסוף, ויקדים כלתו לאחותו, כי היכי דתיהוי אחות אשה לבסוף:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:5:1.english: This clause - Let him teach the entire prohibition of [sisters] at the end, and place his daughter-in-law before his sister, so that a wife’s sister will be at the end.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:5:2.english: Closeness, closeness - Those who are closer to him, he listed first.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:5:3.english: For [they are] his own relatives - And among all of them, there are no relatives like these.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:6:1.hebrew: למטה דידה - דאשתו, ואע"ג דהנך לאו משום קורבה דידיה אסירן ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:6:1.english: Below her - [That is,] of his wife; and even though these are not forbidden to him on account of his own kinship [to them].

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:6:2.hebrew: למעלה דידה - חמותו. ולמעלה דידיה לא מצי למיתני מידי, דהא אמו לא אתיא ליה לייבום, שהרי אסורה לאחיו מאביו משום אשת אביו:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:6:2.english: Above her - [I.e.,] his mother-in-law. And [as for generations] above him, [the Tanna] could not teach anything, for his mother cannot come to him for levirate marriage, as she is forbidden to his paternal brother as his father's wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:7:1.hebrew: ותני אחותו ואחות אמו דקרובי עצמו - טפי מכלתו, דכלתו לאו קרובתו היא, אלא מכח קדושי בנו נאסרה עליו:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:7:1.english: And he taught his sister and his mother's sister, who are his own relatives - More so than his daughter-in-law, for his daughter-in-law is not his [blood] relative, but rather she was forbidden to him by virtue of his son's betrothal.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:7:2.hebrew: ובדין הוא דליקדמה לכלתו מקמי אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו דלאו משום קורבא הוא דאסור - כלומר: וכיון דקרובין נקט ואזיל, וכלתו ואשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו ואשת אחיו מאמו לאו משום קורבא דידיה הוא דאסירן ליה — בדין הוא דליתני כלתו מקמי אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, ומקמי אשת אחיו מאמו נמי, משום דכלתו חמירא טפי מנייהו, והוה ליה למנקט חומרי, כיון דלא מצי למינקט קורבי:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:7:2.english: And by right he should have preceded his daughter-in-law before the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist, as it is not due to closeness of relation that she is forbidden - That is to say: Since [the Tanna] was proceeding by [order of] relatives, and his daughter-in-law, the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist, and the wife of his maternal brother are not forbidden to him on account of their relationship to him — by right he should have taught his daughter-in-law before the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist, and before the wife of his maternal brother as well, because his daughter-in-law is more severe than them, and he should have proceeded by severity, since he could not proceed by closeness of relation.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:8:1.hebrew: מאי איריא דקתני פוטרות - דמשמע פטורות הן, ואי בעי מייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:8:1.english: Why does [the tanna] specifically teach "they exempt" - For it implies that they are [merely] exempt, and if he wishes, he may enter into levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:8:2.hebrew: ליתני אסורות - דהא ודאי אסורות הן, מאחר שאינן זקוקות לייבום וקיימי באיסור אשת אח:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:8:2.english: Let him teach: They are forbidden - For indeed, they are certainly forbidden, since they are not bound to levirate marriage and remain under the prohibition of a brother's wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:8:3.hebrew: ה"א אוסרות - לייבום. וחליצה לא משתמעא מהכא, שאין איסור בחליצה; והוה אמינא: מיחלץ חלצי על כרחו, שאין אשת אח מאב בלא בנים נפטרת בלא חליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:8:3.english: I would say: “They prohibit” - [That is,] for levirate marriage. And chalitzah is not implied from here, for there is no prohibition in chalitzah; and I would say: they must perform chalitzah perforce, for the wife of a paternal brother without children is not released without chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:9:1.hebrew: מאי קעביד - והלכך, לא שייך לשון איסור בחליצה, אלא לשון פטור:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:9:1.english: What has he done? - And therefore, the terminology of prohibition does not apply to ḥalitza, but rather the terminology of exemption.

Rashi on Yevamot 3a:9:2.hebrew: אלמה לא - שייך [לשון] איסור? הא ודאי שייך, שאם אתה אומר חולצת, אתי למימר מתייבמת:
Rashi on Yevamot 3a:9:2.english: Why not? - [Why is the] terminology of prohibition [not] applicable? It certainly is applicable, for if you say she performs ḥalitza, one will come to say she may enter into levirate marriage.

Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:10:1.hebrew: כיון דבמקום מצוה הוא דאסירה צרה - ואי הוה תני "אסורות", הוה משמע כל שכן שלא במקום מצוה, כיון דאיסור צרה מחמת ערוה קאתי. מש"ה קתני "פוטרות" — דהשתא במקום מצוה הוא דאסור, משום דממילא קאי באיסור אשת אח:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:10:1.english: "Since it is in the place of a mitzvah that the rival wife is forbidden" - And if he had taught "are forbidden", it would have implied all the more so where there is no mitzvah, since the prohibition of the rival wife comes on account of the forbidden relative. For this reason he taught "exempt" — for now, it is [only] in the place of a mitzvah that she is forbidden, because she automatically remains under the prohibition of a brother's wife.

Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:12:1.hebrew: דמצות חליצה קודמת - השתא דקתני תרוייהו ושונה חליצה ברישא — משמע דחליצה קודמת; אבל אי לא הוה תני אלא חליצה לחודה — לא הוה משמע מידי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:12:1.english: "That the mitzvah of ḥalitza takes precedence" - Now that [the Mishnah] teaches both of them and teaches ḥalitza first, it implies that [the mitzvah of] ḥalitza takes precedence; but had it taught only ḥalitza alone, it would not have implied anything [regarding precedence].

Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:2:1.hebrew: דאמר רבא אמר לי רב יצחק בר אבדימי - יש מגיהין רב, משום דרב יצחק בר אבדימי היה רבו של רב — כדאמר בפרק כל הבשר (חולין דף קי. ושם): "איכא תנא דאתנייה לרב כחל? אחוי ליה לרב יצחק בר אבדימי"; ובפ' כירה (שבת מ: ושם): "א"ר יצחק בר אבדימי: פעם אחת נכנסתי אחר רבי לבית המרחץ כו'". ולא היה רבא בימיו, דביום שמת רב יהודה נולד רבא, בפ' בתרא דקידושין (ד' עב:). ואר"ת דע"כ גרסי' הכא רבא, שהיה בר פלוגתיה דאביי; ואמר בפ' הנשרפין (סנהדרין עו.): "בתו מאנוסתו מנלן? אמר אביי: ק"ו — על בת בתו ענש, על בתו לא כ"ש? רבא אמר: רב יצחק בר אבדימי כו'". וצ"ל דתרי יצחק בר אבדימי היו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:2:1.english: "For Rava said: Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said to me" - Some emend [the text to read] "Rav", because Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi was Rav's teacher — as [the Gemara] says in the chapter "Kol HaBasar" (Chullin 110a and there): "Is there a Tanna who taught Rav [to permit eating] an udder? He pointed out Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi to him"; and in the chapter "Kira" (Shabbat 40b and there): "Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said: Once I entered the bathhouse after Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi], etc." And Rava was not [alive] in his days, for on the day that Rav Yehudah died, Rava was born, [as stated] in the last chapter of Kiddushin (72b). And Rabbeinu Tam says that perforce we must read "Rava" here, for he was the disputant of Abaye; and [the Gemara] says in the chapter "HaNisrafin" (Sanhedrin 76a): "From where do we derive [the prohibition against having relations with] his daughter from a woman he raped? Abaye said: [It is derived by] an a fortiori inference: If regarding his daughter's daughter [the Torah] punished, regarding his daughter is it not all the more so? Rava said: Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi [said to me], etc." And it must be said that there were two [sages named] Yitzḥak bar Avdimi.

Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:7:1.hebrew: מקמי אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו - וה"ה מקמי אשת אחיו מאמו, וחדא מנייהו נקט; דתרוייהו לאו קרובי עצמו נינהו אלא ע"י קידושין, וכלתו שהיא אשת בנו קרובה מנייהו טפי. אבל אין לומר: דוקא לגבי אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו כלתו קרובה טפי, לפי שלא היה בעולמו, אבל לגבי אשת אחיו מאמו לא, דבאשת בנו איפלג דרא, כדאשכחן לענין עדות בב"ב (ד' קכח.) דאפי' מאן דמכשר באבא דאבא פסיל בן אחיו — דע"כ לענין עריות אשת בנו קרובה טפי מאשת אח, שהבן כרעיה דאבוה הוא, דקחשיב בתו ובת בתו קרובי עצמו טפי מאחותו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:7:1.english: "Before the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist" - And the same applies [that the Tanna should have taught his daughter-in-law] before the wife of his maternal brother, and [the Gemara] cited [only] one of them; for both of them are not his own blood relatives, but rather [relatives] through marriage, and his daughter-in-law, who is his son's wife, is more closely related than they are. However, one cannot say that specifically with regard to the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist, his daughter-in-law is more closely related because [that brother] did not coexist with him, but with regard to the wife of his maternal brother [she is] not [closer], since in the case of his son's wife the generation is divided — as we find with regard to testimony in Bava Batra (128a) that even the one who validates [testimony regarding] a father's father disqualifies a brother's son — for perforce, with regard to forbidden relations, a son's wife is more closely related than a brother's wife, because a son is [considered as] his father's leg [i.e., an extension of the father himself], for [the Tanna] considers his daughter and daughter's daughter closer relatives to himself than his sister.

Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:8:1.hebrew: מאי איריא דתנא פוטרות - פי', דמשמע: אבל אי בעי מייבם, ליתני אסורות לייבם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:8:1.english: "Why does [the tanna] specifically teach 'they exempt'?" - Explanation: For [the word "exempt"] implies: but if he wishes, he may perform levirate marriage; [therefore,] let [the tanna] teach: "They are forbidden to perform levirate marriage."

Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:8:2.hebrew: אבל מיחלץ חלצה קמ"ל - אע"ג דמסיפא שמעינן דברישא לא בעיא חליצה, דקתני בסיפא: "כל שיכולה למאן" כו' — מ"מ ניחא ליה נמי לאשמועינן ברישא גופיה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3a:8:2.english: "But she must perform ḥalitza, [therefore] it teaches us" - Even though from the seifa we would learn that in the reisha she does not require ḥalitza — as it teaches in the seifa: "Anyone who is able to refuse [through mi'un]..." etc. — nevertheless, [the tanna] preferred to also teach us [this] in the reisha itself.
